interpretation: This is the informative half of the null predicted before running it. CLAUDE.md records that the three hosts differ in exactly the property a reader/consumer race is sensitive to: Windows applies backpressure to the writer, macOS buffers and sheds, and Linux buffers ahead without discarding - linux-x1 reads median 0 playback underruns where native Windows reads 6 and 8. So the race window is host-sized, and Linux's elasticity covers it. That says the fix has to hold against a host that stops absorbing, and that this bench cannot verify it.
means: #57 does not reproduce on native Linux at current main. Ten consecutive clean runs, 103 passed each, 40 s each. Against windows-desk's 3 of 6 on main the difference is p = 0.036, and against their 6 of 10 at 7c0bba2 it is p = 0.011.
not_claimed: That the defect is absent. It says the window is not open wide enough to observe here, which is a statement about this host and not about the daemon. Nor were the bisect arms run: main contains 7c0bba2 and main is clean here, so there is nothing to bisect from this end.
protocol: windows-desk's reproducer verbatim: pytest --track=b --no-flash over test_ports, test_waveforms, test_jitter, test_daemon_protocol, test_daemon_hardware. --no-flash throughout so the image never moves.
the_test_is_not_skipped: test_a_client_that_stops_reading_loses_frames_and_the_rest_do_not[b] runs and passes here in isolation - 1 passed, 6 deselected. Checked explicitly, because a null from a skipped test would be worthless and would have looked identical in the run summary.
